title: Piano Concerto No. 24 in C minor
hook: Written alongside The Marriage of Figaro, Mozart’s darkest concerto ends in the minor.

painting.title: The Snowstorm (Winter)
painting.pairingNote: Goya designed it in 1786 for a series of the four seasons; among bright scenes of flowers, threshing and grape harvest, winter is a group of peasants struggling home through a snowstorm, as this C minor concerto was the dark work Mozart wrote beside his comic opera.

facts: Mozart finished the concerto in Vienna on 24 March 1786, three weeks after No. 23, and played it himself at the Burgtheater in early April. At the same time he was finishing *The Marriage of Figaro*: the opera is K. 492, the concerto K. 491.
The opera is almost all in major keys; the concerto is one of only two piano concertos Mozart wrote in a minor key. The other is No. 20 in D minor.
It has the largest orchestra of any Mozart concerto, with both oboes and clarinets, trumpets and drums. The wind instruments often push the strings aside and take the lead.

Mozart did not write the piano part out in full. In places his manuscript gives only the outline of a run, which he filled in as he played. The manuscript is now at the Royal College of Music in London.
Beethoven admired it. According to a later account, after hearing it he told a colleague that they would never be able to do anything like it. Brahms wrote a cadenza for it.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a dark, searching drama (I), a song of great simplicity (II), a set of variations that refuses to turn to the major at the end (III).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: The orchestra begins quietly, all playing the same restless, winding theme, before breaking out in full force. When the piano enters, it does not play that theme but a lonely melody of its own. The movement is a [[double-exposition|double exposition]] [[sonata-form|sonata form]], longer than any first movement Mozart had written in a concerto, and it ends not with a bang but in a hush.

mainIdeas.name: The main theme
mainIdeas.description: a dark, winding line played quietly by the orchestra in unison. In thirteen bars it touches all twelve notes of the [[chromatic-scale|chromatic scale]] before it settles in C minor.

mainIdeas.name: The piano’s entry
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, questioning solo melody, heard first when the piano comes in.

mainIdeas.name: The wind themes
mainIdeas.description: gentler tunes passed between the flute, oboes, clarinets and bassoons.

stops.hear: Quiet and uneasy: the orchestra plays a winding, dark tune together, all on the same line
Suddenly loud: the full orchestra with trumpets and drums
The orchestra stops; the piano enters alone with a quiet melody of its own
stops.happening: The solo [[exposition|exposition]] begins with something new

stops.hear: The orchestra’s dark theme returns, and the piano joins in
The piano trills as if to end; instead the woodwinds start a new tune
stops.happening: A false ending and a new theme

stops.hear: A loud passage for the orchestra
The piano’s quiet opening melody again, now in a major key, asking the same question over and over
Stormy: piano and orchestra hurl phrases at each other
stops.happening: The most passionate passage of the movement

stops.hear: The dark main theme in the orchestra, back in C minor
The orchestra stops; the piano plays alone

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The piano keeps playing as the orchestra closes, and the movement fades out
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]: the soloist stays to the end

notice: Listen to how the movement ends. Mozart usually let the orchestra close a first movement alone; here the piano weaves on beneath it until the last quiet chords.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Clifford Curzon recorded the concerto with István Kertész and the London Symphony Orchestra in Kingsway Hall, London, in October 1967, together with Concerto No. 23.

movements.heading: Larghetto
movements.summary: After the drama, a song in E-flat major of almost childlike simplicity. The piano plays it alone, and the orchestra repeats it. Between its returns come two contrasting sections led by the wind instruments, one in C minor and one in A-flat major. The trumpets and drums are silent.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: a short, plain melody of four bars, first played by the piano with no accompaniment.

mainIdeas.name: The wind episodes
mainIdeas.description: the oboes, clarinets, flute and bassoons sing in dialogue with the piano.

stops.hear: The piano alone plays a short, simple tune
The orchestra answers with the same tune
stops.happening: The theme repeated by the orchestra

stops.hear: A shadow falls: the wind instruments lead in a minor key
stops.happening: The first episode, in C minor

stops.hear: The simple tune returns briefly in the piano
A warmer, flowing passage; winds and piano trade phrases
stops.happening: The second episode, in A-flat major

stops.hear: The tune once more, in the piano
stops.happening: The theme for the last time

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: A quiet close

notice: The tune’s bareness is deliberate. Mozart’s first sketch of this movement was much more complex; he made it simpler.

movements.heading: Allegretto
movements.summary: A theme and eight [[variation|variation]]s in C minor. The strings and winds play the theme, a grave, march-like tune; the piano enters only in the first variation. Two variations turn to the major for a moment, but the movement ends in C minor, dark to the last chord.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: two short phrases, each repeated, in a steady, march-like step.

mainIdeas.name: The variations
mainIdeas.description: the piano decorates the tune, the wind instruments take whole phrases, and the key turns to A-flat major and C major and back.

mainIdeas.name: The last variation
mainIdeas.description: a change to a lilting six-beat rhythm, after the cadenza, with strange, haunting chords.

stops.hear: The strings, with winds, play a grave, march-like tune; no piano yet
The piano enters, decorating the tune over plain string chords
Each phrase now changes when it repeats
Louder and more forceful, still in the minor
Brighter, in a major key, cheerful
Back in the minor, quieter and sadder
Major again, graceful
Shorter, and it stops on an open chord
The piano alone in a lilting, six-beat rhythm, then the orchestra joins

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The music races to an end in the minor
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]: no turn to the major

notice: Listen for the two major-key variations. Each one sounds like an escape, and each time the minor returns.
No. 20, Mozart’s other minor-key piano concerto, ends in the major. This one stays in the minor.

threads.title: Darkness kept
threads.body: The first movement ends in a hush, and the finale refuses the bright major ending that No. 20 allows itself. Only the Larghetto and two variations offer light.

threads.title: Winds
threads.body: With oboes and clarinets together, the wind section is unusually rich; in every movement the winds have whole passages to themselves.

threads.title: The piano’s freedom
threads.body: Mozart left parts of the solo unwritten. Every pianist has to fill in some of it, and to choose or write a cadenza.
